articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub for the world to see. When the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own secrets, maybe it's time to question who's watching the watchers.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor leaked AWS GovCloud credentials on a public GitHub repo, exposing highly privileged government systems. The irony of America's cybersecurity agency getting pwned by basic OPSEC failure is *chef's kiss* perfect.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google claims API key deletion is immediate, but researcher finds they stay active for 23 minutes post-deletion. Another 'trust us, we're tech giants' moment that aged like milk in the sun.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Flaws, Defender 0-Days, Router Botnets, and Supply Chain Chaos
articles.summary: Trump Mobile website leaked thousands of customer records to anyone who could send a basic HTTP request. Even MAGA grifts can't escape the universal truth that security theatre doesn't stop actual breaches.

articles.title: The Alert Firehose Finally Meets Its Match
articles.summary: Critical Ghost CMS SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-26980) exploited to hijack 700+ sites for ClickFix attacks. When your blogging platform becomes a botnet, you know we're living in the dumbest timeline.

articles.title: The AI security gap nobody wants to admit is already here
articles.summary: TrapDoor campaign poisoned 34+ packages across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io to steal credentials. Supply chain attacks are the new normal, and your dependency manager is basically a slot machine at this point.

articles.title: Hacker Selling 340 Million OnlyFans User Records Built From Old Breaches
articles.summary: Anthropic's AI discovered over 10,000 software vulnerabilities, proving machines are already better at finding our coding sins than we are. The robots aren't coming for our jobs—they're exposing how terrible we are at them.

articles.title: The sandworm malware strikes: How a hacker group stole 4,000 GitHub repositories and exposed the rot at the core of modern software security
articles.summary: Hacker selling 340 million OnlyFans user records compiled from old breaches and public profiles. When your adult content consumption becomes a data broker's side hustle, privacy is truly dead.

articles.title: The Trump Phone Appears to Have Already Leaked Its Customers’ Personal Information Through a Glaring Exploit
articles.summary: TeamPCP breached 4,000 GitHub repositories using a poisoned VS Code extension, exposing the fundamental rot in our software supply chain. Trust nothing, verify everything, especially your favorite IDE plugins.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF releases new guide to fight digital surveillance abuses across the Americas where accountability is a fairy tale. Because apparently we need step-by-step instructions to remember that mass surveillance is bad, actually.
